name: Gallio
role: Proconsul of Achaia who refused to judge Paul
whenBasis: Proconsul of Achaia from mid-AD 51 to mid-52, dated by the Delphi inscription. See the card on the Gallio inscription.
summary: Proconsul of Achaia while Paul was in Corinth. The Jews brought Paul before his judgment seat, charging him with persuading people to worship God contrary to the law. Before Paul could speak, Gallio told them that if this were a crime he would hear them, but since it was a dispute about words and names and their own law, they should settle it themselves. He drove them from the judgment seat. When the crowd beat Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, in front of it, Gallio paid no attention.
body: His refusal leaves Paul free to stay in Corinth for some time.

later.text: A letter of Claudius inscribed at Delphi names “Lucius Junius Gallio, my friend and proconsul of Achaia,” dating his term to AD 51–52. He was the elder brother of the philosopher Seneca.

sources.title: Delphi (Gallio) inscription, Delphi Archaeological Museum, SIG³ 801D
